page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.16-128 is an ARM-based general-purpose compute instance built on the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor architecture. The instance configuration allocates 32 dedicated physical cores across 32 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring predictable single-threaded execution. System memory is sized at 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 4.0 GB per-core ratio that matches standard general-purpose computing requirements.

Hardware accelerators are not present, as the instance features zero GPUs. In addition, the configuration includes no integrated local storage, requiring persistent workloads to rely on remote block storage solutions. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The ARM64 architecture delivers consistent thread-level predictability due to dedicated physical core allocation, avoiding multi-tenant core contention or hyperthreading overhead.

From an architectural standpoint, the AmpereOne-M platform provides high core density and efficient resource utilization, yielding strong operational cost efficiency for scale-out microservices and continuous processing tasks. With 32 dedicated cores and 128.0 GB of memory, this instance is suitable for web serving fleets, enterprise application tiers, containerized application runtimes, and distributed continuous integration pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.16-128 is an ARM-based virtual machine featuring the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family. It provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs without multithreading, delivering predictable compute performance alongside 128.0 GB of system memory, which maintains a balanced 4.0 GB RAM allocation per core. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units and features no onboard local disk storage, depending entirely on networked block storage for persistent operational volumes. One complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the instance. Because of its dedicated core structure and 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration, the platform achieves high efficiency for scale-out enterprise workloads. It is suited for running multi-tiered web servers, microservice clusters, development environments, and containerized business applications requiring consistent execution across high-density ARM64 environments.
